title: Preview and Incubating Features knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Preview and Incubating Features” in the supplied Java curriculum?
options: Enabling preview features during compilation and execution
questions.explanation: The supplied PDF lists “Meaning of preview features” under lesson 333, “Preview and Incubating Features”.

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with preview and incubating features?
options: Check the matching JDK release notes and treat preview features as version-specific experiments.
Assume the first successful run proves the code is correct.
Change several unrelated parts until the output looks plausible.
Ignore runtime/version requirements if the code looks familiar.
questions.answer_key: Check the matching JDK release notes and treat preview features as version-specific experiments.
questions.explanation: Check the matching JDK release notes and treat preview features as version-specific experiments. A small reproducible test provides stronger evidence than assumption or trial-and-error changes.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest first step when checking an example related to preview and incubating features?
options: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case.
Skip reproducing the behavior and change multiple settings at once.
Trust a screenshot without checking the program or version that produced it.
Disable all validation and error handling.
questions.answer_key: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case.
questions.explanation: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case. This approach makes the result repeatable and helps isolate the cause of a mismatch.
